title: V2.2.3 ENTRY OVERHAUL — bot entry realigned to the validated backtest + shorts-only re-arm cooldown
summary: The live bot's entry had silently drifted loose from the validated strategy: it had NO arm timeout, NO RSI(3) confirmation, and NO weekly-SMA arm gate — so it was taking stale, low-quality signals the backtest never measured (caught via a live ADBE long entered 6 trading days after its oversold signal, after price had already slid $233->$202). A bot-parity backtest quantified the drift: the loose live model ran at 66.1% WR / PF 1.91 vs the validated 71.0% / PF 2.69. The fix restores all three gates AND adds an Alan refinement found by sweep: a SHORTS-ONLY 5-day re-arm cooldown (longs re-arm freely to catch bullish V-shaped recoveries; shorts wait out the recovery so they don't re-fire low-quality counter-trend repeats). The short cooldown has a clean optimum at 5 days (short WR 62.9% -> 72.3%; falls off at 3 and 7). Final config: 3-day arm timeout + RSI(3) + weekly SMA50/200 gate + free-rearm longs / shorts-only 5-day cooldown = 280 trades, 73.9% WR, PF 3.19, +$31,426 — Pareto-dominates v2.2.1 (+$2,091, +0.50 PF, +2.9pp WR) with the short side cleaned up. detectEntrySignal was rewritten as a faithful bar-by-bar replay of the validated arm machine; the scan data fetch was bumped 2y->5y so the weekly-SMA gate (needs ~200 weekly bars) actually applies live. Verified: reproduces the backtest's entries exactly (GOOG, AAPL), and the stale ADBE entry no longer fires. Exit logic (v2.2.1 hybrid TP1/TP2, broker stops) and the v2.2.2 MANUAL-WATCH flag are unchanged. Full investigation: SID/strategy-test-vault/bot-parity-experiment/.

title: MANUAL-WATCH flag (v2.2.2) — bullish-asset short runners flagged for S/R review
summary: No change to how trades fire — a monitoring aid on top of v2.2.1. The bot now flags any open SHORT on a long-term-bullish asset (price > 200-day SMA AND 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA) as MANUAL-WATCH, because on those names the mechanical TP2 has a blind spot: RSI rarely reaches daily oversold before the bounce, and the SMA exit can round-trip to break-even (30% of runners do). Proven by the GOOG 2026-06 trade (runner RSI bottomed at 38.4, never near oversold) and the TP2-RSI experiment (rsi_oversold fired only 6 times across 89 shorts; replacing the SMA exit with RSI-extreme DOUBLED round-trips to BE — rejected). The flag now shows as a pulsing 👁 WATCH · S/R badge on the dashboard position card, prints a ⚠ MANUAL-WATCH line in the bot log, and sends a consolidated Telegram reminder each run. TP1 still banks mechanically; only the runner half needs the eye. Helper: longTermBullish() in bot-sid.js. Catalogue: SID/strategy-test-vault/tp2-rsi-experiment/.

title: V2.2.1 HYBRID launch — broker-managed stops, side-asymmetric TP1 timing
summary: Per-side decomposition of v2.2 revealed an asymmetry: shorts strictly benefit from intraday-touch TP1 (higher WR AND higher PnL), but longs lose $2.3k over 5y because the bullish drift of US equities WORKS FOR longs — letting price close past RSI 50 books a bigger TP1 partial than locking exactly at 50. V2.2.1 routes by side: longs use v2.1 close-based TP1 (RSI ≥ 50 on daily close), shorts use v2.2 intraday-touch TP1 (resting GTC limit at the RSI-50 target price computed via Wilder-RSI inversion). Both sides keep a broker-enforced GTC stop on Alpaca from the moment of entry — replaces v2.1's PDT-immune 'scan daily candle, close at next open' simulation. Sizing now compounds off the internal $9,351.16 ledger (1% risk = $93.51). Backtest gate (tier1, 5y, $200 fixed risk): WR 69.6% → 71.3% (+1.7pp), PF 2.62 → 2.72 (+0.10), Total PnL $29,317 → $29,528 (+$211). Hybrid Pareto-dominates v2.1 on every metric AND recovers $2,163 of the PnL pure v2.2 left on the table. First v2.2.1 entry (PYPL long, 23sh @ $41.40, signal 2026-06-05) opened 2026-06-12. Vault: SID/strategy-test-vault/v2.2.1-hybrid-shorts-intraday/.

title: BE stop direction-aware penny rounding — no more small-loss BE exits
summary: bot-sid.js:931 used Math.round(entry) for the post-TP1 BE stop, which was direction-blind — a long entry of $281.49 rounded DOWN to $281 (tiny loss locked in), and a short entry of $381.84 rounded UP to $382 (tiny loss locked in). Replaced with direction-aware penny rounding: long stop = entry+0.01, short stop = entry−0.01. Every BE stop now locks in ≥1¢/share profit instead of risking a small loss. Existing GOOG position retrofitted from $382 → $381.83. Audit task #11 MED finding resolved.

title: UNH SHORT fired (26sh @ $378.42)
summary: RSI overbought (73.12) episode from 2026-04-17, trigger fired May 26 with RSI 58.1 + MACD both pointing down. Stop $405 (Math.ceil of episode high). Position currently flat, working as designed.

title: manual-trade.js: OCO + safety fallback pattern
summary: Original pattern (TP1 limit + standalone SL) was rejected by Alpaca with 'insufficient qty' because TP1 held half the shares. Now uses OCO bracket for the TP1 half + standalone stop for the runner. Safety fallback places full-position stop if OCO fails. Telegram alerts added.

title: Pine tp2*Be branches now explicitly close
summary: BE stop after TP1 was ghosting on Pine v6, leaving positions stuck IN-RUNNER forever (tp2Hit=true blocked all other exits — irrecoverable deadlock). Mirror the SMA50/200/Timeout pattern: cancel BE + strategy.close + flag.

title: GHA cron one-shot pattern replaces local scheduler
summary: Manual trades now fire from GitHub runners via cron with date-guards, not via Claude Code's local scheduled-tasks (which required PC to be on). Cloud-first architecture restored.

title: Pine pitfall catalog established
summary: Root CLAUDE.md now hosts a cross-strategy Pine bug catalog (10 entries) with back-refs to detailed write-ups in each strategy's memory. Memory-update convention requires any new Pine fix to append a row here.

title: First live paper trade: GOOG short fired
summary: Regular bot run picked up GOOG short (26sh @ $381.84, stop $405). 9-day signal-to-entry episode with the May 18 $404.47 high becoming the stop. PDT-immune by design — bot manages stops internally.

title: Pine info table now renders on 1D
summary: barstate.islast was not firing on UNH 1D (worked on 4h). Broadened gate to barstate.islast OR barstate.islastconfirmedhistory OR bar_index >= last_bar_index - 1. Confirmed via data_get_pine_tables MCP query.

title: Pine three-layer safety force-close
summary: Stuck-runner positions opened before the entryBarIdx variable existed had it as na, so the 90-bar safety check never fired. Now triple-layer: init entryBarIdx if na + safety on barsSinceEntry + safety on barsSinceTp1.

title: bot-sid.js scan path: 6mo → 2y daily lookback
summary: Default fetchDailyCandles range was 6mo (~125-130 daily bars → ~26-28 weekly bars after resample, below the 30-bar minimum for the weekly check). 9 AUTO-tier tickers were silently rejected with 'insufficient weekly history'. Fix: explicit '2y' on the scan path.

title: Pine strategy.close() blocked by pending strategy.exit()
summary: After TP1 set a BE stop via strategy.exit, the BE order hung on the entry and blocked all subsequent strategy.close() calls — positions stuck IN RUNNER from decades ago, locking the strategy slot. Fix: cancel BE exit BEFORE every strategy.close() in TP2 branches.

title: V2.1 Dynamic TP1+TP2 launch (paper)
summary: Two-stage exit: TP1 closes 50% at RSI 50 and moves stop to break-even; TP2 closes runner on BE / SMA50 / SMA200 / 30-bar timeout. Backtest: 302 trades, 69.5% WR, PF 2.55, +$28k over 5y at fixed $200 risk. v2.0 single-exit toggle preserved (SID_DYNAMIC_TP=false).

title: V2.1 backtest warmup bug fixed
summary: main() was downloading only 5y of price data — Wilder RSI and weekly resamples weren't seasoned at the start of the trade window, silently rejecting ~75% of signals in years 1-3. Now downloads HISTORY_WARMUP_DAYS + BACKTEST_YEARS, filters trades after warmup ends.
